catalogs.title: System contracts
catalogs.description: Device lifecycle, IO, power, and H-bridge operations exposed by the system-contracts interface class.

one_of.description: Disables automatic handling for this device.
Handles only low-severity device errors.
Handles low and medium-severity device errors.
Handles low through high-severity device errors.
Handles every device error severity.
Reads whether the pin is on or off - use for buttons, switches, and sensors that output a simple on/off signal
Same as Input, but reads "on" by default when nothing is connected - use when your button/switch connects the pin to ground when pressed
Same as Input, but reads "off" by default when nothing is connected - use when your button/switch connects the pin to power when pressed
Standard output - the pin can actively switch between on and off. Use this for most outputs like LEDs and relays

A weaker output that can only actively pull the signal to "off" - something else (an external resistor, or the Open-Drain-Pullup option) is needed to make it read "on". Mainly used when several devices need to share the same wire
Same as Open-Drain, but with a built-in helper enabled so the pin reads "on" by itself instead of needing an extra part
Rapidly switches the pin on and off to fake an in-between level - use to dim an LED or control a motor's speed
Measures the exact voltage on the pin instead of just on/off - use to read sensors that report a varying value, like a potentiometer or a temperature sensor
Outputs an exact, steady voltage level instead of just on/off - the opposite of ADC
Don't watch this pin for changes - nothing gets triggered
Triggers the instant the pin switches from off to on
Triggers the instant the pin switches from on to off
Triggers on any change - whether the pin switches from off to on, or on to off
Triggers when the measured value leaves the safe/expected range you set - use to catch a value going too high or too low
Triggers when the measured value comes back into the range you set - use to catch when a value returns to normal
A fixed voltage.
Programmable voltage within a range (standard power range, up to 21 V).
Adjustable voltage within a range (extended power range, up to 28 V).
Current draw is approaching the limit - not cut off yet, just a heads-up
Current draw exceeded the limit - output is protected/shut down
Not identified; the budget uses the measured input voltage and the board's assumed current
USB-C Power Delivery; the budget uses the input voltage and the source's current
External supply; the budget uses the input voltage and the current entered by the user
Battery; the budget uses the measured voltage, current limited only by the board
The voltage went above the safe limit
The voltage dropped below the safe limit
A short circuit was detected on the output
Current draw is approaching the limit - not cut off yet, just a heads-up
Current draw exceeded the limit - output is protected/shut down
The device got too hot and triggered thermal protection
The battery charge fell to the low threshold
The battery charge fell to the critical threshold
The power source can no longer cover what the outputs are set to draw
The board switched to another power source (the value is the new source)
Only raise the event
Suspend the affected output: that rail, or every rail for a board-level event
Reset the affected device: that rail, or every rail for a board-level event
Stop the program and suspend every device
Bidirectional drive from -1.0 to 1.0
High-side PWM drive from 0.0 to 1.0
Low-side PWM sink from 0.0 to 1.0

catalogs.title: Events
catalogs.description: Link events (pin changes, power alerts, motor faults, connection changes) to the program and to actions.

one_of.description: Pin interrupts and analog alerts. Channel = pin, event = the edge or window crossed, value = level or mV
Regulator, monitor and board power events. Event = power event; board events use device 255
Motor driver faults. Channel = bridge channel, event = fault reason, value = current in mA
Connection events. Event = BLE event
Events raised by features. Device = feature ID

event.note: per source: IO edge / window, power event, H-bridge fault, BLE event; 255 = any
